field_semantics.candidate_sigma_injective: Whether this row itself proposes the SGGM labeling sigma and, if so, whether that labeling is injective. Null means not a sigma proposal.
field_semantics.candidate_star_axioms: Properties of a proposed free partial binary star only. Null means the row is not a star proposal or the property is not proved. These fields never describe mere determinism of unary readouts or the charged group oracle.
field_semantics.delta: The constrained-label density in the published model; null means no bound is supplied.

model.source: Corrigan-Gibbs, Henzinger, and Wu, The Structured Generic-Group Model, EUROCRYPT 2026
model.structured_operation: a partial single-valued binary function star : L x L -> L
model.cost_measure: Each group addition is a charged group-oracle query. Negation and known-scalar multiplication are derived using charged queries (typically O(log q) for scalar multiplication), not free primitives. Only star and local computation are free.
model.lower_bound_scope: a hard distribution of structured labelings, not automatically one fixed concrete coordinate encoding
model.prime_order_bound: Omega(min(sqrt(q), 1/delta)) under the paper's exact assumptions

conclusions.known: The published SGGM theorem applies only after an explicit structured label space, injective structured labeling, compatible partial star, and theorem-specific distribution are supplied.
conclusions.reproduced: Repository theorems establish secp256k1_pointX_not_injective using the distinct witnesses G and -G, and the M16 projective bridge records two-output Kummer addition semantics.
conclusions.derived: The naive assignments sigma(a) = pointX([a]G) and star = the Kummer-output S3/H relation fail injectivity and single-valuedness respectively.
conclusions.refuted: The published SGGM lower bound applies through the specific naive sigma(a) = pointX([a]G), star = Kummer-output S3/H map.
conclusions.unknown: Whether any other injective label space and partial star faithfully simulate the complete M16 pipeline and satisfy the published theorem, or whether a relational extension admits a comparable useful lower bound.

claim_boundary: This artifact proves no lower bound against representation-aware secp256k1 ECDLP, no solver lower bound, and no attack. It refutes one naive model map only; broader SGGM applicability remains unestablished.
